answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake in a cipher-backed escrow before it may trade. Newcomers start with zero reputation and only tiny transaction limits; trust grows through verified, paid work over time, not through sheer numbers. Colluding clones then face a summit of costs: every fake identity needs its own stake, its own history, and forfeits the deposit if caught double-spending. Honest agents keep their stake and earn fees, so the market becomes an oasis where real work is cheaper than forgery.
